species: Multiple (Tyrannosauridae, Hadrosauridae, Ornithomimidae, Ankylosauridae, Pachycephalosauridae, Small Theropoda, Ceratopsia)
pose: An expansive landscape composition showcasing an extraordinarily rich and historically accurate ecosystem representing the ultimate collection of distinct dinosaur clades arrayed across a vibrant Late Cretaceous delta floodplain. In the immediate foreground, a heavily armored ankylosaur (Ankylosaurus) stands firmly with its low, wide, bone-plated back and clubbed tail visible. On the opposite side of the foreground, a dome-headed pachycephalosaur (Pachycephalosaurus) is depicted in profile, showcasing its unique spiked, thickened skull roof as it navigates the dense ferns. Along the sunny, wide riverbanks of the midground, a herd of long-billed hadrosaurs (Edmontosaurus) gather to drink, while a robust, low-slung ceratopsian (Triceratops) guards the adjacent riverbank in a stable three-quarter profile view. Across the open sandbanks nearby, a slender, bird-like ornithomimid (Struthiomimus) is captured mid-sprint alongside a small, hyper-alert theropod darting through the low brush. Anchoring the deep background along a distant, hazy river ridge, the commanding silhouette of a massive large theropod (Tyrannosaurus) watches over the entire active, crowded floodplain under a high-key, sun-drenched sky with stylized palm-like trees.
